title: Lesson 11 - Data Governance Basics: Tags, Classifications, and Metadata
description: Apply data governance requirements to platform configuration, focused on tagging and classifying data objects and fields so policy-based governance applies at scale.

questions.question: A consultant must protect every field that holds a Social Security Number, including fields added next year, without editing permissions each time. What is the right approach?
options: Tag the SSN fields and write a policy keyed on that tag
Set each field's permissions manually every quarter
Hide the entire object in the data model
Rely on the data space prefix to block access
questions.explanation: Tagging the fields and keying a policy on the tag means new fields tagged the same way are protected automatically. Hiding the whole object is the strongest distractor and is wrong because it is far broader than the requirement and blocks legitimate access to non-sensitive fields.

questions.question: An admin tries to delete a tag and the platform blocks it. What is the most likely reason?
options: The tag has too many child tags
The tag is used in a policy
The tag API name is auto-filled
The tag is object level rather than field level
questions.explanation: Tags in use by a policy cannot be deleted until they are removed from the policy. Having many children is the strongest distractor and is wrong because tag hierarchy depth does not block deletion.

questions.question: Which statement about tag hierarchy in Data 360 is correct?
options: A tag can have one parent and multiple children, limited to one level
A tag can have multiple parents
Tags cannot have children at all
questions.explanation: A tag may have a single parent and multiple children, and the hierarchy stops at one level. Unlimited nesting is the strongest distractor and is wrong because the platform enforces a single level of depth.
